This number defines the overall specifications for the panelboard as a complete unit.

B: Indicates it is a Main Breaker unit (factory installed) rather than "Main Lug Only" (MLO).

This is not a collection of yellowed, folded attic papers. Every piece in this set has been preserved in clean, unread, flawless condition for over 40 years. It tells the complete story of the 1985 title—from the pre-series preview to the Game 7 victory celebrations.
What Is Included in This 5-Piece Collection:
Sports Illustrated (Nov. 4, 1985) - "A Royal Crown" (2 COPIES): Two separate, pristine copies of the famous championship issue. Both are rare NEWSSTAND EDITIONS with no subscriber mailing labels printed on the covers. Perfect for having one copy on display while keeping the second stored or submitted for grading.
Sports Illustrated (Oct. 28, 1985) - "The World Series / Ozzie Smith": The official World Series Preview issue printed right before Game 1. Also an unprinted newsstand copy with razor-sharp edges and bright cover inks.
The Kansas City Star (Oct. 28, 1985) - "World Champions!": The iconic morning-after newspaper wrap. Features clean white pages, zero sun fading, and no dark fold creases across the headline. Includes all original 1985 local ads inside.
The Squire’s Other Paper (Oct. 31, 1985) - "Free At Last!": An ultra-rare local Kansas City suburban newspaper printed right after Game 7. Because this publisher went out of print years ago, surviving copies in this unread condition are almost impossible to find anywhere on the market today.
Why This Set Is Unique:
Buying these items individually in this condition requires months of searching and multiple shipping fees. This listing offers a complete, pre-curated 1985 time capsule ready for custom framing, a home sports room, or an executive office display. Would make a unique gift for a Royal's fan.

A very rare find and piece of Kansas City history.  A near new section of unused hard maple commercial butcher block counter top that is at least 63 years old. Koch was a major manufacturer of butcher shop equipment, and based here in the Kansas City area.

Rucksack Compatibility
Our standard of compatibility is that Ruck Plates will be stable and secure in your Ruck with minimal shifting.
If you have a Ruck Plate Carrier, we recommend the shorter (Standard) Ruck Plates -  10LB, 20LB or 30LB.
The 20L and 25L Rucker feature an additional pocket to securely fit a 45LB Ruck Plate, which can be paired with a 20LB or 30LB Ruck Plate for up to 75 lbs of total weight.

Start With 20#
The relationship between your body, the weight, and the rucksack will determine your level of comfort on the move. Our recommendation for most people is to start with 20 lbs of weight for rucking, progress in increments of ~10 lbs, and ultimately max out at 1/3 of your bodyweight. title: Antique UPRR train track level inclinometer Union Pacific Rail Road rr
ai_notes: [Antique UPRR railroad track level] A niche antique item with no price listed. Value is highly subjective to collectors.
description:
This is a very cool vintage railroad level for checking the grade or pitch on the train tracks as they were laid.
Other inclinometers that I have had were fancy models and in great condition and I assume they were gently used by an inspector.
This one has been well used although still in great shape. The condition makes me imagine that it was carried and used as the tracks were laid.
It’s marked UPRR in two places. It’s my understanding that Union Pacific used the UPRR designation until they were done building the Transcontinental Railroad in the mid/late 1800s so this is a very old piece of history. They then changed the name to Union Pacific Railway and used the UPR designation.
It’s also marked with what looks like EV. 6- 66 and the brass level bubble is marked Empire 58”R
It measures 62 1/2” long and the brass elevation ruler is graduated up to 7”
This is an awesome piece of railroading and American history and will make a very nice addition to your collection.
If you know of a nice train museum please let me know or show them this ad and have them contact me.
Thanks

title: Antique UPRR train track level inclinometer Union Pacific Rail Road rr
ai_notes: [Antique UPRR train track level] Collectible railroad tool, price not specified.
description:
This is a very cool vintage railroad level for checking the grade or pitch on the train tracks as they were laid.
Other inclinometers that I have had were fancy models and in great condition and I assume they were gently used by an inspector.
This one has been well used although still in great shape. The condition makes me imagine that it was carried and used as the tracks were laid.
It’s marked UPRR in two places. It’s my understanding that Union Pacific used the UPRR designation until they were done building the Transcontinental Railroad in the mid/late 1800s so this is a very old piece of history. They then changed the name to Union Pacific Railway and used the UPR designation.
It’s also marked with what looks like EV. 6- 66 and the brass level bubble is marked Empire 58”R
It measures 62 1/2” long and the brass elevation ruler is graduated up to 7”
This is an awesome piece of railroading and American history and will make a very nice addition to your collection.
If you know of a nice train museum please let me know or show them this ad and have them contact me.
Thanks

description:

title: Antique UPRR train track level inclinometer Union Pacific Rail Road rr
ai_notes: [Antique UPRR railroad track inclinometer] This is a niche antique railroad tool. Pricing is unknown as it is a unique historical collectible with no standard retail equivalent.
description:
This is a very cool vintage railroad level for checking the grade or pitch on the train tracks as they were laid.
Other inclinometers that I have had were fancy models and in great condition and I assume they were gently used by an inspector.
This one has been well used although still in great shape. The condition makes me imagine that it was carried and used as the tracks were laid.
It’s marked UPRR in two places. It’s my understanding that Union Pacific used the UPRR designation until they were done building the Transcontinental Railroad in the mid/late 1800s so this is a very old piece of history. They then changed the name to Union Pacific Railway and used the UPR designation.
It’s also marked with what looks like EV. 6- 66 and the brass level bubble is marked Empire 58”R
It measures 62 1/2” long and the brass elevation ruler is graduated up to 7”
This is an awesome piece of railroading and American history and will make a very nice addition to your collection.
If you know of a nice train museum please let me know or show them this ad and have them contact me.

title: Antique UPRR train track level inclinometer Union Pacific Rail Road rr
ai_notes: [Antique UPRR train track inclinometer] Niche historical railroad collectible; no price provided.
description:
This is a very cool vintage railroad level for checking the grade or pitch on the train tracks as they were laid.
Other inclinometers that I have had were fancy models and in great condition and I assume they were gently used by an inspector.
This one has been well used although still in great shape. The condition makes me imagine that it was carried and used as the tracks were laid.
It’s marked UPRR in two places. It’s my understanding that Union Pacific used the UPRR designation until they were done building the Transcontinental Railroad in the mid/late 1800s so this is a very old piece of history. They then changed the name to Union Pacific Railway and used the UPR designation.
It’s also marked with what looks like EV. 6- 66 and the brass level bubble is marked Empire 58”R
It measures 62 1/2” long and the brass elevation ruler is graduated up to 7”
This is an awesome piece of railroading and American history and will make a very nice addition to your collection.
If you know of a nice train museum please let me know or show them this ad and have them contact me.
